title: Sinai Wilderness
subtitle: Wilderness travel explorer - schematic environment, not a route reconstruction
summary: An evidence-aware wilderness experience for topography, water stress, travel scale, and the limits of route reconstruction. It does not identify Mount Sinai or any Exodus station.
disclaimer: Schematic environmental reconstruction based on broad arid-landscape characteristics and the textual wilderness setting. No depicted ridge, wadi, campsite, water source, route, or mountain is presented as the biblical location; site-specific terrain and paleoenvironment data remain pending primary-source verification.

evidenceLegend.label: Schematic reconstruction
evidenceLegend.description: Project-authored visual scaffolding used to test the scene engine; not a claim about a specific historical view.

evidenceLegend.label: Regional travel context
evidenceLegend.description: Broad discussion of arid travel geography may be historically useful while remaining non-site-specific.

evidenceLegend.label: Unknown / disputed
evidenceLegend.description: Mount Sinai's modern location is not securely identified and competing proposal families remain separate.

periods.label: Exodus narrative context
periods.note: Narrative-context mode only; this prototype does not assign a precise archaeological date to the Exodus.

panorama.alt: Schematic mountainous wilderness panorama illustrating travel constraints without identifying an Exodus route or Mount Sinai

hotspots.label: Mount Sinai remains unlocated
hotspots.summary: The biblical mountain is central to Exodus, but the atlas does not assign the biblical Mount Sinai a normal map coordinate.

whyShown.evidence: The biblical text identifies a covenant mountain but does not provide a modern coordinate.
whyShown.inference: This schematic ridge communicates mountainous wilderness only; it is not an identification.
whyShown.alternatives: Southern Sinai tradition, northern/central Sinai or Negev proposals, and northwestern Arabia proposals remain distinct candidate families.

hotspots.label: Travel through arid terrain
hotspots.summary: V2 scenes can explain slope, exposure, route difficulty, and water constraints without drawing a falsely exact itinerary.

whyShown.evidence: The narrative repeatedly describes wilderness travel and water stress.
whyShown.inference: Regional terrain and hydrology can illuminate travel constraints without proving a route.
whyShown.alternatives: Future scene packs should compare route families and hydrological reconstructions rather than merge them into one path.

hotspots.label: Reconstruction boundary
hotspots.summary: The rendered foreground is intentionally generic and is tagged as artistic reconstruction rather than archaeological evidence.

whyShown.evidence: No site-specific archaeological dataset is bundled with this engine prototype.
whyShown.inference: The visual layers exist to validate panorama movement, hotspot anchoring, and evidence labeling.
whyShown.alternatives: A release-quality Sinai scene should substitute verified DEM, imagery, geology, and paleoenvironment sources with explicit licenses and uncertainty notes.

hotspots.label: Water stations: text known, sites unknown
hotspots.summary: Marah, Elim, and Rephidim structure the biblical itinerary, but their modern locations are not securely identified.

whyShown.evidence: The itinerary explicitly names water-related wilderness stations and episodes.
whyShown.inference: Water availability is a legitimate travel-geography question, but a generic oasis or wadi image cannot identify Marah, Elim, or Rephidim.
whyShown.alternatives: Candidate oases and route models should be introduced only as separately sourced proposals rather than silently embedded in the landscape.
